index_removal_events.reason_summary: Dow Chemical and historical DuPont merged into DowDuPont; original DD shareholders receive merger consideration, not a bankruptcy wipeout.
S&P cited evolving economic and sector representation and the small price weight of GE. Index deletion is not an exchange delisting.
DowDuPont split into three companies; the index selected the new Dow for Materials exposure. DWDP is the merger successor of original DD, so track in the DD lineage, not as a new original asset.
Apple 4-for-1 split reduced Information Technology price weight; replacements also diversify economic and sector exposure.
Part of the same three-constituent adjustment prompted by Apple split and broader representation.
RTX is original UTX after April 2020 name/ticker change. Part of the same three-constituent adjustment.
Walmart 3-for-1 split reduced its price weight; Amazon increased retail and broader business exposure. WBA entered after the 2015 base date and is not an original asset.
More representative semiconductor exposure; persistently low-priced stocks have small price weights.
More representative Materials exposure; Dow was the smallest DJIA member by company market capitalization. DOW entered in 2019, but is a DD shareholder-lineage descendant.
Verizon had about 0.5% index weight due to its low price; Alphabet broadens Communication Services and digital-business representation.

security_identity_notes.summary: Merger effective August 31, 2017. Historical EID common shares exchanged for 1.2820 DWDP shares plus cash in lieu of fractional shares. Old DD shares suspended before September 1 open; DWDP trading starts September 1. This is not current DD continuously existing since 2015.

DowDuPont subsequently renamed DuPont de Nemours and began trading under DD on June 3, 2019 following 2019 separations. DD shareholder-return lineage must also account for DOW/CTVA distributions and later corporate actions. The complete shareholder basket and latest descendants are assigned to a separate corporate-action audit.

After Carrier/Otis spin-offs and the merger, United Technologies shareholders continued holding their existing common shares. UTX changed name and ticker to Raytheon Technologies/RTX. Old RTN ceased trading and converted to UTC common, not the reverse.
Removing GE from the index does not justify removing its original shareholder lineage or adding WBA. GE distributions and subsequent spin-offs belong in the separate corporate-action audit.

current_endpoint_reconciliation.scope_limit: Endpoint reconciliation and targeted searches found no additional roster differences. This is not an independently exhaustive day-by-day archive proof of no intermediate removal/re-entry.

interpretation.recommended_report_sentence: We fix the investable universe using the Dow Jones Industrial Average constituents observed on 31 October 2015 and retain the original shareholder lineages after subsequent index removals. This mitigates selection based on end-of-sample survivors and winners, but does not establish that all survivorship or selection biases are eliminated.
forbidden_inferences: Index deletion means bankruptcy or exchange delisting.
Current DD ticker identifies the same original 2015 security throughout.
UTX common shares were canceled like the acquired RTN shares.
Replacing removed original names with new Dow entrants preserves the fixed 2015 cohort.
A historical Dow roster guarantees representative bankrupt-company exposure or eliminates survivorship bias.
